title: Big Plate House (Give It A Good Old Rub)
The Rub
style: Euphoric hard house remix, festival dance, 150 BPM, Eb major, four-on-the-floor kick, offbeat bass, bright supersaw chords, pitched-up sing-along vocal hook, crowd chant, build-up and drop, club anthe
lyrics:
[verse]
One pea, forty quid, give it a good old rub
One plate, full size, that's how I get it done

[build]
Big plate, big plate, hands in the air
Big plate, big plate, feel the sound

[chorus]
Give it a good old rub, give it a good old rub
Give it a good old rub, give it a good old rub
We belong in the crowd, we belong in the sound
Big plate, big plate, we never stop around

[drop]
Give it a good old rub
Rub it, rub it, rub it
Big plate, big plate, feel the beat
Give it a good old rub

title: Slow Sunday Gravy
style: slow warm northern soul, brass, Rhodes piano, brushed drums, gravelly friendly male vocal, Sunday afternoon mood
lyrics:
[verse]
Pot on the hob since the morning light
Windows all steamed and the kettle's on
Pea's by the door with his nose held high
Waiting on a Sunday that lasts all day
[chorus]
Slow Sunday gravy, pour it thick
Big plate, warm plate, take your time
Slow Sunday gravy, no one's rushing
Everyone's welcome, there's more in the pot
[verse]
Roast on the table and the neighbours in
Nobody counts what's on their plate
Seconds are coming and thirds are too
That's how a Sunday ought to be
[chorus]
Slow Sunday gravy, pour it thick
Big plate, warm plate, take your time
Slow Sunday gravy, no one's rushing
Everyone's welcome, there's more in the pot

title: Bonfire Night Bounce
style: Uptempo northern soul stomp, handclaps, brass stabs, warm male singalong vocal, crackly bonfire feel
lyrics: [verse] Cold November, sparks in the sky / Sausage on a stick and a pie piled high / Nobody's counting, nobody's small / Big old plate for one and all [chorus] Bring a sausage to the fire / Raise it up a little higher / Give it a good old rub / Warm hands, warm hearts, big grub [drop] hey! hey! bonfire bounce

title: Four Corners
style: UK garage / dance, 130bpm, four-on-the-floor kick, deep sub bass, four corner-lamp pulses (orange blue pink green), warm male baritone, playful and punchy
lyrics:
[verse]
Orange on the left, blue on the right
Pink is in the corner, green is in the night
Two feet on the floor, keep the rhythm alive
Big plate in the corner, let the whole village dive

[chorus]
Four corners, four lights, give it a good old rub
Dance floor, dance floor, let the rhythm come up
I don't want a small plate, I want a proper beat
Rub the floor, rub the floor, till the night's complete

[drop]
(orange-blue-pink-green pulse, sub bass, kick four to the floor)

[chorus]
Four corners, four lights, give it a good old rub
Dance floor, dance floor, let the rhythm come up
I don't want a small plate, I want a proper beat
Rub the floor, rub the floor, till the night's complete

title: The Rub in a Jar
style: UK garage, 130bpm, four-corner-lamp bounce, deep sub bass, sharp hi-hats, warm male vocal in a dry close-mic, slightly reverb-washed. A little soul, a little funk, a lot of moustache.
lyrics:
[verse]
A visitor asked if I sell anything
I said no, then I thought about it all the way home
Twenty pieces I'd put my name to
And I can say in a sentence what a Barry drawing is

[build]
Warm light in a dark place
A real word on a hand-painted sign
The dog in the frame
Food on a BIG plate

[chorus]
The rub in a jar
Give it a good old rub
The rub in a jar
Give it a good old rub
Not yet, but the stall is coming
John's sorting the practical side

[drop]
(beat drop, four-corner-lamp bounce, sub bass heavy)
(beat drop, four-corner-lamp bounce, sub bass heavy)
(beat drop, four-corner-lamp bounce, sub bass heavy)
(beat drop, four-corner-lamp bounce, sub bass heavy)

title: The Rub of the Sea
style: Sea shanty, 108 bpm, D major, male baritone vocal with gang call-and-response "hey-ho", fiddle and tuba, ship-bell percussion, big warm chorus, slightly ragged handclap on the offbeat
lyrics:
[verse]
I left the kitchen in a fog of steam
With forty deckchairs on the lorry beam
The pie was still hot and the moustache was wide
And the Big Plate village was on the tide
[build]
Haul the rail! (hey-ho)
Pull the coach! (hey-ho)
Give the wheel a good old rub
And a proper plate of fish and chips
[chorus]
Oh the rub of the sea, the rub of the sea
It rolls down the harbour like a big plate pie
The lamps are burning, the floor is spinning
And the moon is a pie in the sky
[verse]
Now the railway runs where the lorry ran
And the platform's long with a ticket in hand
Every coach is a kitchen, every wheel is a pot
And the whole village hums like a jukebox hot
[build]
Haul the rail! (hey-ho)
Pull the coach! (hey-ho)
Give the wheel a good old rub
And a proper plate of fish and chips
[chorus]
Oh the rub of the sea, the rub of the sea
It rolls down the harbour like a big plate pie
The lamps are burning, the floor is spinning
And the moon is a pie in the sky
[drop]
Hey-ho! (hey-ho!)
Rub the wheel! (hey-ho!)
Big plate! (hey-ho!)
Come hungry!
[chorus]
Oh the rub of the sea, the rub of the sea
It rolls down the harbour like a big plate pie
The lamps are burning, the floor is spinning
And the moon is a pie in the sky

title: Pea Goes To Sleep
style: gentle lullaby, music box and soft acoustic guitar, warm brushed drums, tender northern male vocal, hushed and sleepy
lyrics:
[verse]
The lamps are low on Main Street, the oven's going cold
The pies are in the window and the big plate's put away
Pea's by the fire with a smudge of green on his nose
Dreaming of a sausage as long as the railway

[chorus]
Sleep now, little Pea, sleep now, good old lad
Tomorrow there'll be gravy and the best day you've had
Sleep now, little Pea, give it a good old rub
Night night, little dog, from your big old Barry

[verse]
The trains are in the station, the deckchairs are in rows
The moon is on the dance floor and nobody's there
Pea's by the fire with his paws going twitch, twitch
Chasing a cabbage the size of a house

[chorus]
Sleep now, little Pea, sleep now, good old lad
Tomorrow there'll be gravy and the best day you've had
Sleep now, little Pea, give it a good old rub
Night night, little dog, from your big old Barry

title: Barry's Big Plate Reggae
style: Reggae — one-drop bass, skank guitar, organ stab, warm male vocal, "one pea forty quid" hook, laid-back 75 bpm, key of G major
lyrics:
[verse]
One pea on a plate, forty quid to pay
I looked at the menu and I felt like I'd say
Give it a good old rub, that's the way
Big plate, big portion, don't take it away

[chorus]
Big plate, big plate, that's what I want
Not a little bit, not a tiny scrap
Big plate, big plate, give it a rub
That's the only way that a chef can work

[verse]
I built a whole village because I got fed up
With the small plates and the overpriced stuff
Now I've got my own kitchen, my own dance floor
And a whole lot of room to fill my soul

[chorus]
Big plate, big plate, that's what I want
Not a little bit, not a tiny scrap
Big plate, big plate, give it a rub
That's the only way that a chef can work

title: A Dog's Place
style: Slow soul, brushed drums, warm upright bass, muted trumpet, baritone male vocal, 72 bpm, key of E minor — a quiet lullaby for a village that's seen a lot
lyrics:
[verse]
The bonfire's cold and the sky's the colour of wet stone
The grill's gone quiet, the plates are left on the bone
And the dog's got his bed in the brown by the door
And he don't need the whole village to want him more

[chorus]
Give a dog his place, give a dog his name
A roof over his head and a warm little flame
You can rub what you've got, but you can't rub a home
So build him a kennel and let him sleep in it, home

[verse]
One pea, forty quid, the world's gone small and thin
But the ground is big and the grass lets him in
He's not on the plate, he's the one who eats
And he don't judge the moustache, not one of the beats

[chorus]
Give a dog his place, give a dog his name
A roof over his head and a warm little flame
You can rub what you've got, but you can't rub a home
So build him a kennel and let him sleep in it, home

[drop]
(soft)
Sleep, little dog, the village's still
The lamps are low and the bonfire's chill
The door's left open, the sign says mind
And the moustache's resting, and the night's kind

title: The Tune on the Heap
style: Folk-club: fingerpicked acoustic guitar, low cello drone, brushed snare, a warm male baritone with a little gravel — the sound of a busker's last note hanging in cold air, half-remembered.
lyrics:
[verse]
A hat on the pavement, a coin in the wind,
A tune I can't name and I don't know where it's been,
He played it like he'd known it for a hundred years,
Then turned up a corner with no second ear.

[chorus]
So I'll keep the sound in a little brass ball,
Set it down on the heap where the wind can tell all,
Some tunes you can't hold, you can only keep,
A coin in the pocket of something you sleep.

[verse]
I woke with the melody stuck to my teeth,
Like gravy on a spoon after a long day's feast,
I've got the words in the kitchen but not the name,
And the moustache is full of the same old flame.

[chorus]
So I'll keep the sound in a little brass ball,
Set it down on the heap where the wind can tell all,
Some tunes you can't hold, you can only keep,
A coin in the pocket of something you sleep.
